A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same deep α-stable kernel research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–J are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendices H–J report original simulation and UCI regression results, including prediction errors, coverage, timings and posterior feature distributions.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds an α sensitivity study and posterior-kernel analyses in Appendices H.3.3–H.3.4.

M1.justification: The network construction, stable scale mixtures, recursive kernels, posterior prediction procedure and MCMC Algorithms 1–3 are unchanged. The new α sweep evaluates the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions use discontinuous regression simulations in one, two and ten dimensions and the Boston, Energy and Yacht datasets. The added analyses reuse existing tasks and data scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain DIWP, NNGP, GP Bayes, GP MLE and Stable. Stable remains restricted to the one- and two-dimensional simulations; no evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Appendix H.3.3 adds a separate evaluation across α = 0.5, 1, 1.5, 1.95 and 1.99 on a 1,000-point prediction grid. Existing experiments retain their splits, metrics, training budgets and depth settings.

E4.justification: New Appendix H.3.3 tests prediction sensitivity to α, while H.3.4 examines posterior-kernel variability in the existing one- and two-dimensional examples. These are focused additions to the retained depth, information-decay, coverage and feature analyses.

E5.justification: v2 adds 25th–75th percentile predictive bands for the α sweep and 25th, 50th and 75th kernel-posterior quantiles. Existing standard-deviation reporting, 90% intervals and stated run/split counts are unchanged.

E6.justification: New Figures 6–7 report increased smoothing and generally wider predictive intervals near α = 2, and nondegenerate kernel-posterior quantiles. Figure 1 also has revised non-Gaussian traces with the same decay ordering. Existing tabulated errors, timings and coverage values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorems, propositions, kernel formulas and mathematical material in Appendices A–G are unchanged. The added pointer to Cho and Saul's Equation (4) supplies a reference for an existing computation, not a new derivation.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the deep α-stable limit, stochastic kernels permitting feature learning, tractable posterior inference and empirical benefits. The new appendix evidence supports these retained claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: The introduction qualifies the zero-output-covariance limitation by specifying i.i.d. weights and an isotropic Gaussian limit. New discussion interprets kernel quantiles as evidence of heavy tails and nondegeneracy, and proposes broader activations and a speculative heavy-tailed NTK extension.

D1.justification: Section 2 newly provides a repository link described as containing a full implementation with examples, and identifies the source equation for computing Jδ. This adds reproducibility information without changing the documented algorithms.

R1.justification: v2 adds Tsuchida et al. (2019, 2021), Jacot et al. (2018) and Simsekli et al. (2019), connecting the work to related conditional Gaussian representations, broader activations and possible heavy-tailed NTKs. The principal research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: There are localized abstract, introduction and conclusion expansions, two new appendix subsections, acknowledgments and publication/affiliation updates. Most prose and the overall section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 6–7, corrects Figure 1's axis and caption to conditional mutual information, and adjusts Figure 2's formatting. Existing Energy and Boston feature plots exchange main-text and appendix placement; subsequent figures are renumbered.

improvement.justification: The α sensitivity study and direct kernel-posterior visualizations strengthen evidence for existing claims. Added code-access information, more precise Gaussian-limit qualifications and clearer figure labeling improve transparency. These are limited gains: the core theory and benchmark tables remain unchanged, and the NTK extension is still speculative.
